stages.explanation: Writing one inbox entry per member is too expensive for big rooms. Inbox workers are idempotent per (user, conversation, seq), so redelivered batches are safe. Fan-out moves behind a queue, and very large rooms switch to pull from the log, trading a second read path for bounded write amplification. [Idempotence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Idempotence) means repeating the same logical operation does not repeat its effect.

stages.explanation: Inboxes grow without bound; old tokens must still work or fail clearly. A token older than retention gets an explicit resync response, never a silent gap. Compaction keeps inboxes small; a device with an expired token resyncs from the log, which remains the source of truth. [Time to live](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time_to_live) defines when a value or right stops being valid. Expiration must be checked at the point of use, even when background cleanup runs later.
